topic: Registration Process for Annual Charity Bicycle Tour

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You will hear a talk by an organisation representative at a meeting about a charity event.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: First, you have some time to read through questions one to four.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions one to four.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for coming to this Ann-Marie charity member meeting. I'm so pleased to see so many members here tonight, and I always appreciate your generosity, compassion and concern.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: I know you are eager to hear about our institution's progress. Our annual charity bicycle tour raises money for medical research at the London Children's Hospital.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: Each year, a group of generous individuals dedicates ten days to cycling around England to raise both funds and awareness. And might I say that it's a fun time as well.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: Now, I know some of you are interested in participating and want to know how you can get involved. Well, it is fairly easy.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: First, you must register for the event, which you can do on the charity's website.
transcript.highlight_text: you can do on the charity's website.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: You don't even have to visit our office. After that, you'll be asked to sign a form on which you will give us an estimate of how much money you plan to raise.
transcript.highlight_text: you will give us an estimate of how much money you plan to raise.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: We recommend our participants attempt to raise a minimum of £3,000, but we certainly encourage you to raise more than that.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: Next, you will need to find sponsors who agree to donate a predetermined amount of money to you should you finish the tour.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: It's always a good idea to start with friends and family first, but many participants have also raised funds from local businesses.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: And then you have to show up for the tour on June 12 at 6am with your bicycle, gear and equipment.
transcript.highlight_text: with your bicycle, gear and equipment.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: You don't have to worry about bringing any documents, although something proving your identity might be helpful. I'll hand out a leaflet that will tell you everything you need to know.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: And you will also be given a number to pin onto the back of your shirt. This will allow us to track who successfully finishes.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: And once you've completed the tour, collect the donations from your various sponsors and give them to us by June 26.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: Finally, the charity will provide you with receipts by the end of June. You can give these to people who ask for them for tax purposes.
transcript.highlight_text: the charity will provide you with receipts

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: It's mid-March now, so that means you have plenty of time to find sponsors. And we do offer support in the way of informational brochures.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: And of course, we will always be here to answer your questions or respond to your concerns.

transcript.speaker: Representative
transcript.text: Now, before we go on to the next topic of discussion, are there any questions about this year's charity tour?

transcript.text: You now have 15 seconds to check your answers.
